#### Correction (closure of the shape theorem, Paper 47 §20, 159 pp.)

**The scale of the margin was overstated in the phase 191–192 sections of this README.** What is PROVED is
λ_A(T) ≤ 4·10⁹·T·e^{−15.449T} (thm:margin, cor:margin1): simple exponential. The doubly exponential scale exp(−e^{(2−ε)T})
or exp(−13e^{2T}) is only Zhu's conjectural law / the NUMERICAL pattern from phase 187, and is not used in any proof. The
clause "it is not an estimate" remains in the paper as `lem:shape-est`: (i) PROVED with the correct margin bound; (ii)
exact Schur reductions with a finite complement inherit the margin (PROVED), with the infinite collar space (Lemma S)
ARGUED; (iii) CONDITIONAL on κ_T ≠ 0; (iv) the general reading "no estimate works" remains ARGUED, not PROVED.
"It is not an identity valid for every comb": `lem:shape-ident`, PROVED. Problem (R) gains clause (11): the sign step
has to be ζ-specific by construction.

#### GUIDING PRINCIPLE (marked by the author as vital)

**The sign has to come from the semiring (ℕ, +, ·): from the interaction between sum and product.** A purely
multiplicative property is not enough (G1, PROVED: the free monoid ℕ^× is indistinguishable from Beurling and from the ideal
monoids of any field → survives O11/O12); a purely additive one is not enough either (comb-generic / generic FE-class: Poisson
over ℤ + Γ holds for Epstein, CA_C_007). The near-coincidences m ≈ kn (residue R9, problem (S)) are exactly the place where
additive proximity meets multiplicative structure. Geometric side (CA_F_003, gap G-F): a ℤ-polarized object whose
positivity comes from amplitude/Riemann–Roch and not from the signature of 𝔞_T — in Weil over 𝔽_q it is C×C, where + and · interact via
Frobenius. **Every new seed must state how it uses the +/· interaction and why it is not purely a monoid property nor purely additive.**

The sphere-packing method rests on (V1) discrete primal with exact attainment, (V2) Poisson combs positive on
both sides, (V3) Fourier eigenfunction structure via modular forms; row D lacks all three in the window LP.

#### Phase 193, front M — problem on prime sites: 0 admissible. CORRECTS THE GUIDING PRINCIPLE

- **Exact form on prime sites (PROVED):** Near = Σ_h C_s(h), Chen-type correlations of p with p−h = p′q^a, over ALL
  shifts |h| ≲ 2T₀p; it encodes the first-moment Hardy–Littlewood for (x, qx+h), NOT twin primes, Goldbach, or k-tuples.
- **Site arithmetic carries no information (PROVED):** parity and residues are reindexings of Near = Σ_q Near_q (linear
  in Λ, each Near_q of trace 0 → indefinite). **Thm 3.1/Cor 3.2:** any real set of sites with ratios → 1 is decisive;
  the statement "∀M" on primes is equivalent to the same statement on sites p+θ_p with independent irrational θ_p, where x − nx′ is
  never an integer → parity, residues, singular series, Chen switching, sieve and parity DO NOT EVEN EXIST, and the truth value is the
  same. Bounded-shift configurations (twins/Chen) have weight 0 in the decisive configurations.
- **Anti-diamagnetism = exact cancellation (PROVED):** m(τ) + 2Re(ζ′/ζ)(½+iτ) = 0 for every real τ outside the ordinates of zeros
  (FE + reality of ξ; new for all τ, previously only τ=0). The primes contribute no surplus: they cancel C₀ exactly; it holds for
  the entire class with FE.
- **CORRECTION TO THE GUIDING PRINCIPLE:** the "+" in p − n·p′ is cosmetic. The only +/· content is that of the comb's
  positions log n with weights v_n (successor property (S⁺), CA_H_002), which is independent of the sites. The principle now reads: the sign
  would have to come from the structure of the comb on log ℕ (positions + weights) read through the form, without going through
  site arithmetic or symbol densities (which cancel exactly) — and everything that is not that belongs to the zero side.

## IV — `01_PROGRAMS_RH1-RH5.md`

### Route index — 01-context/RH1..RH5 (prior programs 2017–2021)

Scope: 01-context/RH{1..5}/README.md + all task*/OVERVIEW.md (RH1 89, RH2 94, RH3 83, RH4 83, RH5 60 tasks). Paths relative to 01-context/.
Common object: truncated Dirichlet polynomial D_F(t;N)=Σ_{n≤N} a_n n^{-1/2-it}, ω-strata S_k (ω(n)=k), controls ζ, L(χ mod 4/5), random multiplicative f_rand, Liouville λ, Möbius μ, Davenport–Heilbronn L_DH (and ε-perturbations), explicit violators F12/F14/F16, modular L(Δ,s), Maass F13, deformation ζ_δ.
General verdict: none of RH1–RH4 carries a sign/positivity statement; all are NUMERICAL-ONLY phenomenology on finite partial sums. Only RH5 touches Weil-type quadratic forms directly.

Tool families: [RES] resonance/large values; [OMEGA] ω-class/multiplicative decomposition; [EVS] extreme-value statistics (GEV/Gumbel); [RMM] random multiplicative models; [COEF] coefficient-architecture/sign structure; [CLS] ML classification/detectors; [MOM] moments; [PRET] pretentious distance; [CAL] DH/violator calibration; [EF] explicit-formula injection/forward sensitivity; [ISP] inverse spectral/Hilbert–Pólya/Jacobi; [POS] positivity criteria (Weil/Li/GORZ/kernel matrices); [STAT] zero statistics/TDA.

extensions; HP = Hilbert–Pólya / spectral realization / OS; CCM = Connes–Consani–Moscovici prolate/spectral
triples & finite-section convergence; FRED = Fredholm / determinants / adjugates / Feshbach / Toeplitz-GLT;

DIOPH = Diophantine / Baker / Kronecker; ERG = almost-periodicity / universality / Tauberian / averaging;
PHYS = physics models / quantum imports; STAT = statistics / TDA / numerics detectors; LOCAL = per-place /
Hasse–Minkowski / adelic factorization; IDX = index theory / Maslov / signed index; FRAME = sampling,
frames, Fourier interpolation.

## IV — `06_OPEN_RESIDUES_DEAD_SUBROUTES.md`

### 06 — Open residues of row D: dead sub-routes and admissible directions


REF-D = "the sub-route ends in an internal reformulation of D". It records where a sub-route ends; it does not close the residue.
Labels: PROVED / CITED / CONDITIONAL / ARGUED / OPEN / NO-GO / FALSIFIED / NUMÉRICO.
Sources: README "Residuos vivos"; 01–05; SYNTHESIS_188 (Updates 1–3); NT_SYNTHESIS; adversarial reviews 188 (N_011, L2_018, L2_021, L2_023,
L2_024_025) and 189 (NT_001_004, NT_005_007, NT_008_010, NT_011_014); Paper 47 §sec:open; master grid R162_2300 (live cells = rows tagged
OPEN-RESIDUE in 04_, 93 rows).
Abbreviations: P47 = 04-papers/47-row-d-dual-certificates/main.tex; 188/ = 03-research/phase-188-closing-D/; 189/ = 03-research/phase-189-new-theory/;
186/ = 03-research/phase-186-toolbox/.

**Barriers that every residue must escape.** Each admissible direction below lists the ones it must escape.
- **[void]** cor:void / thm:finmod (P47): classes closed under finite deletion Λ1_{n≥N} or one-term amplification Λ+c1_{n=n₀}.
- **[tail]** W-tail (N_003; P47 cor:wtail): any comb with a = Λ on n<n₀ and 0 ≤ a ≤ Λ.
- **[sens]** prop:wit-sens: bounded functionals of the weights (a 1e-5 perturbation flips the sign).
- **[F]** F-uniform falsifiers: M_m quartets, f_t, Λ̃, DH/Epstein, ζ̃ = ζ·R (NT_011), a_P, Poisson combs.
- **[T1/T2]** field-uniformity (ζ_K, S₃) and A1–A6 (Epstein).
- **[lin/det/fam/pat/loc/mom/coh]** W-walls (R186; P47 §barriers).
- **[margin]** P47 cor:margin1: λ_A ≤ 4·10⁹ T exp(−15.449T), T≥1 (PROVED). The doubly exponential estimate cited in P47 rem:moriceiling concerns λ_W, is recorded there as unverified, and must not be transferred to λ_A (λ_W≤λ_A has the wrong direction for that transfer). See AUDIT_207_001 and P47 thm:margin with its proof.
- **[opcalc]** prop:opcalc / N_018 meta: linear identities + Bochner/C–S only.
- **[zeros]** zero-information class C_zeros: zero-free regions, density, finite zero sets (thm:finZ).
- **[crit]** exact criticality: centre, packets, mean square (L2_010, N_013, L2_019).
- **[sym]** FE antisymmetry D_{1−σ} = −D_σ (L2_026).

**Statement.** For every T and every F ∈ P_T: Σ_n v_n Re c_F(log n) ≤ 𝔞_∞(F), with v_n = 2Λ(n)n^{−1/2}. Polar-free form: 𝓕_T(F) ≤ 𝔞^♯(F), where
λ^♯(T) ↓ C₀+4 (N_001, P47 prop:sharp). Nyquist form: the coherence 𝒞_T(ω_k) is signed against the samples |F̂(ω_k)|², ω_k = πk/2T (P47 (N)).
(L2) ⟺ (N_loc) (L2_006).
**Status.** OPEN. Main frontier (SYNTHESIS_188 §4.1).

#### R2. (Ω₀): clamped ground-state test
**Statement.** For every T > ½log5: Σ_n 2Λ(n)n^{−½}h_T(log n) < 0, where h_T is the clamped bending ground mode of P_T = (¼−∂²)H²₀
(ĥ_T ≥ 0, double zeros at ±i/2) (L2_008–009).
**Status.** OPEN. Necessary for (L2) at each T, not sufficient (L2_007 §3; rem:bar-loc). The reduction 𝒯₀ ⟺ (Ω₀) is PROVED.
**Dead sub-routes.** PNT-type error terms (cor:void, L2_009 §1(i)); finitely many zeros (§1(ii), thm:finZ); local symbol argument (W-loc);
Tate-free localization (L2_004).
**Admissible directions.** One explicit Weil sum per window, using an individual property of Λ that finite modifications preserving PNT lack.
Must escape: [void], [tail], [zeros]. Nothing has been tried beyond the class statements above.

**Statement.** sup_{T,F}(𝓕_T − 𝔞^♯)₊/G_κ < ∞. Equivalently, along λ_t = (1−t)ρ_κ + tΛ with κ > κ*, t_∞ := lim t*(T) > 0 (N_012).
The target is t_∞ = 1 (REF-D). t_∞ > 0 is implied by the target (D ⇒ (Ω_{t₀}), PROVED); whether it is strictly weaker is OPEN (K12_DAMPED_001 Lemma 2.1: (Ω_{t₀}) is invariant under finite comb modifications, so it does not imply D; the dichotomy t_∞ ∈ {0,1} is ARGUED — AUDIT_204_TRACT_E_001).
**Status.** OPEN.

#### R4. (Ω_Φ): global fixed-point residual
**Statement.** Find a functional inequality controlling the window negativity of a comb λ by its Poisson–Euler residual r(λ) = λ − Φ(λ). Λ is a
fixed point of Φ (N_009; uniqueness CONDITIONAL on Hamburger).
**Status.** OPEN as an obligation, but already treated beyond linearization: phase197 `BARRIER_D2_001_DEFECT_STABILITY_SPLITTING_AND_CONTINUATION_NO_GO.md` and `AUDIT_197_2.md` examine arbitrary non-linear/global defects and continuation paths.
**Precise audited label.** N_010 §3 treats linearization. The phase197 result is a **PROVED reduction**, not a universal impossibility: a bound vanishing at the actual datum retains the required sign there plus sign-free rigidity. Its audit corrects the factor2 of the weight metric and distinguishes Lipschitz sharpness from the concave-class assertion.
**Admissible directions.** Merely saying non-perturbative/non-local is NOT a new hypothesis. A renewed construction must supply an independent signed endpoint or path-remainder estimate beyond the already treated defect/continuation framework. REF-D alone does not close this obligation. Must escape [F], [void], [margin] in the declared class.

#### R5. (E_γ): twisted Chebyshev inequality at one frequency
**Statement.** limsup_T 𝓕_T(F_T)/‖F_T‖² ≤ m^♯(γ) for the concentrating packets at γ. Here m^♯ = Re ψ(5/4+iγ/2) − log π
(exact form, N_001; P47 prop:Egamma-exact). D ⇒ (E_γ) is PROVED (R186_050; P47 prop:wit-Egamma).
**Status.** OPEN. The packet limit equals m^♯(γ) exactly, so the inequality is critical at every γ (N_013).
**Dead sub-routes.** Weakening by a constant (E_γ,C) collapses to (E_γ) (N_013, CONDITIONAL); large sieve and VK are insufficient (R186_051);
centre γ=0 is exactly critical (L2_010); no F-uniform bound (N_001).
**Admissible directions.** An exponent-½ signed twisted ψ bound at frequency γ. Must escape: [zeros], [crit], [void]. R186_050 §4.3 and N_013
Prop 3.3 read (E_γ) as a zero-side statement, so a prime-side proof must avoid zero-location input.

#### R6. Lower half of the bilateral law
**Statement.** λ_A(T) ≥ L(T)(1−o(1)) with explicit L > 0 (Zhu Conj 12.1, primitive normalization; R186_039 BL). By P47 thm:wit-Tc(iv),
λ_A ≥ −ε(T) with ε → 0 already gives the target. In the stated asymptotic lower bound, any admissible L(T) must satisfy L(T) ≤ (1+o(1))4·10⁹ T exp(−15.449T) by P47 cor:margin1. The cited, unverified doubly exponential ceiling for λ_W is not a proved ceiling for λ_A.
**Status.** OPEN. Not excluded by W-fam (P47 rem:bar-fam). Beyond ½log5 no lower bound better than C₀ − A is known.
**Dead sub-routes.** Landau–Widom main term (predicts β_max > 1: NO-GO, R186_039 §2.3); L_Sh = exp(−cN_Sh log N_Sh) is not bilateral (ARGUED);
pattern fit 13.0e^{2T} (W-pat, NUMÉRICO); f_t and M_m share the law up to a perturbation (R186_039 §3); bounded-range families (W-fam).
**Admissible directions.** An asymptotic in which the sign enters through the lower half, uniformly in T. Must escape: [fam], [pat], [det],
[margin] (the proved exponential ceiling for λ_A), [F] (M_m, f_t).

##### R9 — subruta muerta registrada en la fase 212

- **Fase 212, sistema ampliado de cuadrados con selección o torsión aritmética en nodos o modos — NO-GO con clase, PROVED (relativo a GRAM §18.2 y a la holomorfía de z ↦ P_z de GLOBAL «Escalas libres de cuadrados»).** `ROUND_001_C.md`, Lema 1, Teorema R, Corolario 2; revisión `REVIEW_001_LC.md` (lema de unicidad de coeficientes modales incluido allí). En una identidad única A_0 = Σ cuadrados + resto no negativo sobre el portador de escalas enteras (y = 0), cada cuadrado es continuo en la norma del grafo y sus coeficientes en k son los valores enteros de una función holomorfa de crecimiento polinómico en un semiplano; por tanto ningún cuadrado no nulo puede anularse sobre un conjunto de nodos o de modos de suma recíproca divergente, ni ser la torsión de un funcional continuo por una función con un conjunto de nivel divergente de complemento divergente (caracteres de módulo q ≥ 2, sumas de Ramanujan no constantes, μ, μ², Λ, indicadoras de clases de residuos, de múltiplos o de gcd fijo). Generaliza con el mismo instrumento GRAM §18.7 (soporte finito) y GLOBAL «Escalas libres de cuadrados» (cola libre de cuadrados, discontinuidad de S_sq); lo nuevo es la clase, no la herramienta. No excluye cuadrados continuos con índice o pesos aritméticos en la dilatación, torsiones sin conjunto de nivel divergente, restos sin signo manifiesto, ni objetos por ventana o sobre 𝔸_M. No aporta signo. La dirección de R9 en la formulación (S) queda abierta con una única restricción de módulo de continuidad (Observación 5).

##### B1. Hyperbolic polynomials, Gårding cones, real stability (Borcea–Brändén), MSS interlacing families — score 4
- Mechanism: a polynomial hyperbolic in direction e has a convex Gårding cone; stability is preserved by a classified
  set of linear operators (Borcea–Brändén); interlacing families give "some member beats the expected polynomial".
- Action: the index has the exact separability theorem (frente E, Thm 1: D ⟺ positivity of 𝔞_T on Euler-product vectors
  ⊗_p v_p). The restriction F ↦ 𝔞_T(⊗_p v_p) is multi-affine/multilinear in the per-prime blocks — exactly the object
  Borcea–Brändén/MSS act on, and NOT one-variable real-rootedness (Jensen, closed) nor TP (closed). New reason vs.
  Lee–Yang/Rayleigh (frente J): J used correlation inequalities in a ±1 gauge; here the variables are the prime blocks and
  the question is hyperbolicity of a mixed form, not ferromagnetism.
- Screen: a Borcea–Brändén preserver statement is a class statement → CG unless the preserver uses the window-wise
  vector (Λ(n))_{n<e^{2T}} exactly (cor:shape (a)). Clause 5: the FE enters through the archimedean block, which would
  be one more "variable"; that is the only place the coupling could be non-ζ(½+iτ). Risk: frustration Thm 1.3 may
  imply the multiaffine form is not stable → that itself is a clean NO-GO worth having.
- First theorem: decide whether P_T(z_2,…,z_P) := det or the symbol of 𝔞_T on ⊗_{p≤P} span{1, z_p·e_{log p}} is real
  stable for T = log 2, P = 2,3 (finite, pure algebra); either a stable-preserver structure or an explicit
  non-stability witness tied to the frustrated cycle (m, 2m).

##### B2. Bakry–Émery Γ₂ / curvature–dimension CD(K,N) on the Markov semigroup of frente I — score 4
- Mechanism: Γ₂ ≥ KΓ gives spectral gap ≥ K (lower bound on the bottom), via a *quadratic* (not linear) functional of
  the jump measure J_T.
- Action: frente I proved the form without polar term is Markov (λ₀ < λ_A ≤ λ₂) and that Markov/PF/max principle
  don't decide (O2 conserves them). Γ₂ is not in the index (grep: Bakry absent). Γ₂ of a jump process is bilinear in
  J_T: Γ₂(f) = ∫∫ J(dx)J(dy)(…), so it is non-linear in Λ (clause 1) and is not a cone condition (clause 2).
- Screen: must check whether O2 and (1+c)Λ preserve CD(K) — if yes, NO-GO by thm:shape(A) immediately (cheap screen).
  Rigidity Thm 3 (frente I: FE-symmetric twists lose Markov for T ≥ T_E) hints curvature is FE-sensitive → clause 5.
- First theorem: compute the jump-measure Γ₂ for J_T at T = ½log3, and prove or refute CD(K,∞) with explicit K for
  Λ vs. the falsifiers O2, O4^ε, Beurling.

##### B3. Modular / conformal bootstrap (Hartman–Keller–Stoica, Mazáč analytic functionals, spinning bootstrap) — score 3
- Mechanism: unitarity (positive spectral density) + crossing/modular invariance ⇒ linear functionals with sign give
  bounds; crossing is an exact functional equation coupling light and heavy states.
- Action: the explicit formula is a crossing equation (primes ↔ zeros, FE as S-transform). Clause 5 asks exactly for a
  coupling of small primes with the FE not through ζ(½+iτ): crossing-kernel functionals (Mazáč–Paulos) are such a
  coupling. New vs. frentes L/N: those built *magic functions* (V1–V3) for sphere-packing LPs; HKS-type bounds use the
  *light-spectrum sparseness* hypothesis, which here is "comb supported on log n, n<e^{2T}" (a finite light spectrum).
- Screen: a functional valid for all positive light spectra is CG (B″) and dual-certificate class (D) — likely REF-D.
  Only escape: functionals that use integrality of light dimensions (log n) and conductor 1 jointly (cor:shape (b)).
- First theorem: write 𝔞_T on P_T as a crossing equation with "light sector" {log n: n<e^{2T}}; prove whether an HKS
  universality bound for the heavy sector holds for every comb (then NO-GO, index it) or needs Λ exactly.

##### B4. Proof mining (Kohlenbach) / reverse mathematics of the window statement — score 6 for a meta-result, 0 for sign
- Mechanism: logical metatheorems extract uniform rates from ∀∃ proofs; WP_T is Π⁰₁ for each rational T.
- Action: turns lem:shape-est(iv) ("no estimate carries the sign", ARGUED) into a PROVED statement for proofs in a
  declared formal system (e.g. a monotone functional interpretation would extract a margin ≥ explicit f(T), which
  contradicts thm:margin if f decays slower than e^{−15.449T}). Gives a sign-free but honest closure tool.
- Screen: not a sign carrier; it is a classifier of method classes (closure by impossibility
  within a declared class).
- First theorem: in WKL₀/ACA₀ with an "estimate" schema formalised, any proof of WP_T for all T ∈ [1,2] yields a
  computable margin bound m(T) ≥ g(T) of extractable form; with thm:margin, classify which g are excluded.

##### B5. Resurgence / exact WKB / Stokes constants of the window operator at large T — score 3
- Mechanism: transseries of the bottom eigenvalue; Stokes constants are sign-definite in many integrable problems;
  median resummation preserves reality.
- Action: λ_A(T) ≍ (bounded by) e^{−15.449T} is an exponentially small eigenvalue — the natural object of exact WKB
  (instanton splitting). Archimedean Γ-factor is resurgent (Stirling); prime atoms enter as discrete instantons at
  log n. Clause 5: Stokes data couple the Γ-factor (FE) with atoms log n directly, not through ζ(½+iτ). Not in index
  (WKB/resurg absent; L41 spheroidal asymptotics is only the prolate piece, covered).
- Screen: the leading instanton action is probably comb-generic; sign would sit in a Stokes constant depending on the
  exact vector (Λ(n)) — admissible in shape, unproven to exist.
- First theorem: for the two-atom model (n=2,3, T∈(½log3,½log5)), compute the transseries of the bottom of 𝔞_T and the
  first Stokes constant exactly; test its sign under O2/O4^ε.

## IV — `AUDIT_A.md`

### AUDIT  A — three arXiv papers (adversarial audit)
Sources: arxiv.org/abs pages fetched  (abstract level). Full PDFs were NOT read; every claim below is labelled from the abstract only.


#### 1. arXiv 2602.20313 — W. Michalowski, "On the Pólya Frequency Order of the de Bruijn–Newman Kernel: Certified Failure at Order Five" (v1 , v2 )
- **Statement (abstract):** K(u)=Φ(|u|) (dBN kernel) is not PF₅. Witness: one 5×5 Toeplitz minor det[K(u₀+(i−j)h)] at (u₀,h)=(0.01,0.05) is rigorously negative. PF₄ is left OPEN globally; locally positive at the tested configurations.
- **Method:** 80-digit outward-rounded interval arithmetic; theta-series truncation with proved tail bounds; cross-check by Leibniz expansion plus an independent interval determinant; mpmath ancillary scripts.
- **Correctness (as far as checkable, abstract level):** the claim is finite and falsifiable: one minor, one point, certified enclosure. The method is sound in kind. A small h=0.05 makes the minor nearly singular (Toeplitz minors scale like h^{20}·Wronskian), so the result rests entirely on the interval width. 80 digits is ample if the tail bounds are right. We did not re-run it. Label: **CITED (certified numerics, unrefereed)**.
- **What it implies:** Schoenberg: PF∞ ⇔ 1/𝓛K is Laguerre–Pólya type. PF₅ failure kills every route that needs Φ to be PF_k for k≥5 (PF∞/TP of the kernel, variation-diminishing of order ≥4 for convolution by Φ, Karlin-type sign-regularity of order ≥5). It does NOT touch: PF₄ or lower, Laguerre–Pólya properties of Ξ itself (Ξ in LP class is not equivalent to Φ being PF; Φ is not PF∞, so the de Bruijn/Pólya universal-factor routes run through the Fourier side and not through the kernel's TP), Turán/Jensen-polynomial routes (GORZ), or sign-regularity of Φ on restricted grids.
- **Corpus comparison:** 104_21 shows PF₂ failure for the *prime-exponent lattice law*, which is a different object, so this result is not redundant with it. 104_83 (Ξ Fourier gate) and R155_046/047 (Sturm/nodal, Karlin): this sharpens them by giving a certified ceiling of 4 on the kernel's TP order. R162_1701 §2.4 and R186_041 TP mentions: any step there that assumed TP/PF∞ of Φ is now dead. **Closes more routes: yes, at order ≥5 only.** ⚠ [etiqueta revisada: ver Parte VII.A / Parte VI]

#### 2. arXiv 2609.02882 — Y. Lamzouri, "A new proof that more than 2/3 of the zeros of ζ are simple and on the critical line" (v1 , v2 )
- **Statement:** >67.25% of zeros are simple and on the line; ≥88.76% are simple or on the line.
- **Method:** this is NOT an inertia count. The abstract says it *replaces* the matrix (finite-compression/Sylvester) framework of Alpöge–Furman 2608.13637 with "a single Hilbert-space inequality" plus Montgomery's pair-correlation theorem.
- **Mis-attribution:** the task brief and 05_LITERATURE L52 describe it as "inertia counts on finite compressions". That is wrong for this paper. Only 2608.13637 uses the compression plus Sylvester.
- **Correctness:** it is a streamlined version of a known-to-be-verified result. Label CITED (unrefereed).
- **Relation to Paper 47 Theorem P / thm:index / R186_028:** no inertia number is produced, so it neither agrees with, sharpens, nor contradicts n₋ ≤ 5/7/8 or index one. It is a proportion statement (density), and a proportion is blind to finitely or infinitely many exceptional quartets of density zero. That gives it no purchase on row D, a ∀-test positivity statement. The Hilbert-space inequality is quadratic in a mollified test, which is the same structural position as R184_009 §2(b).

#### 3. arXiv 2609.15329 — A. Pearce-Crump, "Optimising Selberg's method for critical zeros"
- **Statement:** ≥7% of zeros on the line via Selberg's sign-change method (optimised Zhuravlev 1974): closed form for the reciprocal-square-root coefficients, plus PSD mollifiers.
- **Not an inertia paper either.** It is a sign-change counting method. The bound is weaker than Levinson–Conrey, Lamzouri, and Alpöge–Furman. Correctness: plausible, CITED.
- **Relation:** none to Theorem P or thm:index. The one transferable detail is a "PSD mollifier" optimisation, i.e. a positive-semidefinite constraint on mollifier coefficients. The corpus already covers that through the dual-certificate LP/SDP of Paper 47, so it adds nothing.

#### Alpöge–Furman 2608.13637 (context; already audited in R184_009 §2(b))
- Re-stated without the reasoning used in R184_009: on a finite compression, Sylvester inertia counts negative directions. That count is class-blind: the falsifier M_m shifts the index by 4m and the count cannot tell the difference without prior knowledge of the index. A density statement also cannot exclude a density-zero exceptional set, and DH is the separator.
- It is consistent with Theorem P: both bound n₋ of a finite compression from above. Theorem P is archimedean-only per window (n₋(A_∞|P_T) ≤ 5/7/8). AF bounds the off-line contribution on the zero side. Neither contradicts the other, and AF does not sharpen 5/7/8 because it gives no window-indexed count.

#### 1. L55 — Johns, LP slack κ*

**Statements (from 02-setting.tex).**
- Test class: 𝒯 = even, real functions analytic on |Im z| ≤ ½+δ with (1+|z|)²|F| bounded.
- Arch(F) = F(i/2)+F(−i/2)+∫F Ω_∞, where Ω_∞ is the digamma density. **The polar term is part of Arch.**
- Admissible pair: positive measures μ (zero side, even) and ν on [log2/2π, ∞) (prime side) with Arch(F) = ∫F dμ + π⁻¹∫F̂ dν.
- Cone: 𝒞 = {F ≥ 0, F̂ ≥ 0 on [log2/2π, ∞)}. Slack: κ* = inf{Arch(F) : F ∈ 𝒞, ∫F = 1}.
- Thm (duality) [PROVED in paper, standard; the proof route was checked and is sound]: 𝒦 ≠ ∅ ⟺ Arch ≥ 0 on 𝒞 ⟺ the same on Gaussian packets ⟺ κ* ≥ 0. Method: Carathéodory in finite-dimensional sections, a-priori bounds, Helly.
- Prop (floors) [PROVED]: κ* ≥ −1.3231. This is elementary.
- Certified: κ* ≤ 1.4291572·10⁻¹⁰⁶⁰, using Ξ²P_J(t²) with J = 111 prime powers. The certificates vanish at every zero. The proof is computer-assisted; the code was not rerun here (NUMÉRICO for us).
- Unconditional lower bound: κ* ≥ −2.7112·10⁻³, from a certified admissible pair for a slightly larger conductor.
- Theorems B: uniqueness when μ is supported on the ordinates plus 0, or on the ordinates plus summable extra points with ν on the Bondarenko–Radchenko–Seip nodes, or when μ is integer-atomic.

**Correctness.** The parts read are correct and standard: a Delsarte/Odlyzko–Poitou–Serre-type LP. The only nontrivial claims are the numerical certificate and Part II, and neither was re-verified. I found no error in §2.

**Relation to Paper 47.**
- **No overlap in the object.**
  - Johns' κ* is a *linear* program on the whole line with a *fixed* prime gap log 2. It has no window T and no Tate/primitive constraints, and the polar term is inside Arch.
  - Paper 47 def:PD is a *quadratic* (eigenvalue) problem at every window T. The primal is μ = |F̂|²dτ/2π with μ̌ = 0 beyond 2T plus the two polar constraints. The dual consists of signed ν on {|u| ≥ 2T} and β ∈ ℝ².
- **Structural parallels:**
  - (i) Johns' duality theorem ↔ thm:D1 (strong duality, finitely atomic dual sequences). Same Carathéodory/compactness skeleton, different cone.
  - (ii) Johns' certificates Ξ²P_J, which vanish at every zero, ↔ thm:Z (a certificate equals the explicit formula, i.e. a zero-side sum). Johns' certificates are positive on ℝ and not flat-top, so they do not contradict finZ.
  - (iii) The band-limited slice of Johns' cone, with F̂ supported in the gap, is exactly the nonnegative band-limited functions. By Fejér–Riesz/Akhiezer these are the |Ĝ|², i.e. our class at 2T ≤ log 2 **without** the primitive constraints and **with** the polar term. So Johns' statement restricted to the gap is the *complete-form* (non-primitive) version of λ_A(T) ≥ 0 for T ≤ ½log2, which Paper 47 already proves.
- **κ vs κ_⋆: name clash only.** Our κ_⋆ (thm:kappa, sec:combs) is the density threshold for the smooth comb 2κe^{u/2}du to be positive at every window; κ_⋆ ≥ ¼|C₀| > 1. Johns' κ* ≈ 0 is the LP slack. They are not comparable.
- **Usable:**
  - (a) "Certify an admissible *primal* pair for a perturbed conductor to get an unconditional floor" is a primal-side method. Paper 47 has only dual certificates. The analogue would be a lower bound for λ_A via an explicit positive representing pair at a shifted archimedean datum.
  - (b) Hermite interpolation at prime powers as a certificate family. It can be compared with the lattice certificates thm:R / thm:latedge, which pay an O(1/M) edge cost; Johns' family has no window edge because it has no window.
  - Neither touches the sign at T > ½log5.

**Verdict:** parallel and not overlapping, with no error found. Interest: low–medium (tool (a)).

#### 3. L35 — Franchi Viceré, semilocal spectral descent: the flaw

The chain is Thm 1 (CCM 2025 Thm 1.1: σ_S(N,λ) self-adjoint for the inner product QW_λ^N − ε_N⟨·|·⟩, hence real "spectral zeros") → Thm 2 (QW_λ^N(g∗g♯) = Σ g̃(ρ_k) g̃(1−ρ̄_k) = Σ\|g̃(ρ_k)\|² ≥ 0) → Thm 3 (Fejér truncation g_N → g, giving QW_S(g) ≥ 0) → Thm 4 (S ↑ all places) → Weil.

**Flaw 1 (fatal, Thm 2). The ε_N-shift is dropped.**
- ε_N is *defined* as the least eigenvalue of QW_λ^N. So QW_λ^N − ε_N is PSD by definition, and the reality in Thm 1 is a property of that shifted form only.
- Reality of the zeros of the minimal-eigenvector transform does not give QW_λ^N ≥ 0. Indeed QW_λ^N ≥ ε_N, and the sign of ε_N is exactly the open question.
- The displayed "arithmetic–spectral identity" is a finite-dimensional form written as a sum over the spectral zeros of a different operator. Neither CCM §5 nor Connes 1999 Thm 4 contains it in that form. Connes' semilocal trace formula has a remainder, and that remainder is where the sign lives: our phase 183, E_S = Son + R_{S,T}, with n₋(R_{S,T}) = ∞ for T > ½log2 (R183_018 Thm 5.1, R183_019 Thm 4.1).
- So Thm 2 asserts as an identity precisely the step that the phase-183 Sonin NO-GO shows carries no sign.

**Flaw 2 (fatal, Thm 3/4). "QW_S ≥ 0 for each finite S" is false as stated.**
- Take S = {∞}. Then QW_S is the archimedean+polar form, and Paper 47 prop:archneg (PROVED) exhibits a negative vector from T = 0.4608. So a uniform-in-S positivity of semilocal forms is refuted by a single explicit vector. Eberwein §8.1–8.2 report the same numerically.
- Thm 3 also conflates S (places) with the cutoff λ (all primes ≤ λ² enter QW_λ). The "stabilization for λ > M/ε" is only the finite-support statement for fixed g, and it is true but carries no sign.
- In our terms, Theorem X (R186_046) shows that new primes must cancel σ at resolution π/T. The sign lives in the coupling and the complement, not in any S-local block (W-loc, R186_044 Thm 2). Descent "S finite ⟹ S = all" therefore has nothing to transport.

**Flaw 3 (minor).** The numerics (Mathematica, S = {2,3,5,∞}, 4 test functions, 30 zeros) are reported as verifying "Class A" theorems. A form evaluated with zeros on the line is non-negative by construction, so the check is circular.

**Verdict:** NO-GO. The precise failure point is Thm 2: the PSD of QW − ε_N is substituted for the PSD of QW. The failure falls under the phase-183 Sonin wall, prop:archneg, and W-loc.

## IV — `AUDIT_LIU.md`

### Audit : L70 (Liu, "Certified Weil Positivity Beyond the Unit Window")

Read-only audit. Paper 47 not edited.

#### 1. Identification
- Title: "Certified Weil Positivity Beyond the Unit Window: Source-Exact Block-Schur and Tail-Compensation Bounds for the Riemann Zeta Function".
- Author: Vincent Liu (AI-Native Mathematical Research Lab, Taiwan). Manuscript date 14 Sep 2026, alphaXiv posting 15 Sep 2026.
- Location: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.weil-positivity-riemann-zeta-bounds (PDF read in full, 1392 text lines). No arXiv id found.
- Status: "preprint / manuscript under review" (Math. Comp. per the alphaXiv page). The paper itself says alphaXiv is not peer review and that "a public archival identifier and a finalized data/code license have not been supplied". The certificate is NOT publicly reproducible yet. The author declares AI tools (ChatGPT/Codex) as research support.
- Corpus: R186_027 (phase-186-toolbox, row 2) mentions it only for its method (block-Schur, Legendre, rank-two tail), not for its range. Master grid R162_2300 3A has the residual "S5 §5#14: web hit ... sin leer" (OPEN, "could move [compl] endpoint"). That residual is now resolved: it does move the endpoint, CITED.

#### 2. Setting and normalization (Liu §2, eq. (1))
- D_L = C_c^∞((−L,L);ℂ), H_L = L²(−L,L). "Half-width L" = support of f in (−L,L), so supp h_f ⊂ (−2L,2L) and the sum runs over log n < 2L.
- Q(f) = P(f) + (1/2π)∫A(t)|F_f(t)|²dt − Σ c_n H_f(log n), c_n = 2Λ(n)/√n, A(t) = Re ψ(1/4+it/2) − log π, P(f) = 2Re(F_f(i/2)·conj F_f(−i/2)). This is the COMPLETE form (pole term kept, no Tate/pole-vanishing constraint), arbitrary complex tests.
- Thm A: Q ≥ 2^−151‖f‖² on D_1. Thm B: Q ≥ 2^−49162‖f‖² on D_{17/16} (log 8 < 17/8 < log 9; all of 2,3,4,5,7,8 kept). Rigor: interval enclosures + exact integer Gram residual certificates on two 224×224 integer matrices + analytic complement/tail bounds (block-Schur).
- Obstruction theorem: a specified tail-dropping lower comparison has negative high-frequency limit once L > ½log 8 (concerns the comparison, not Q).

Matching with Paper 47: N_T = {n: log n < 2T}, v_n = 2Λ(n)/√n (v_2 = 2log2/√2 matches c_2), F(±i/2) are the Tate moments A, B, so P = 2Re(A B̄) and Q = W_T = 𝔞_T + 2Re(A B̄) on L²(I_T), I_T = [−T,T]. Hence **L = T**. Liu states his normalization agrees with CC21 (149)–(154) and with Zhu; Paper 47 already identifies Zhu's half-width 0.8 with T = 0.8 (main.tex 142, 302–304, 4605, 4656). Liu: the 17/16 window has autocorrelation support 17/8 (L70's "≈ log 8.4" is correct: e^{2.125} ≈ 8.37).
- Domain: Liu's bound is on C_c^∞, Paper 47's λ^W_T is on L²(I_T) (form domain). C_c^∞ is a form core (Liu cites CC23/Suzuki; Paper 47 has its own closure lemmas), so the bound passes to the bottom. Minor check, not a gap.

#### 3. Verdict
If Liu Thm B is correct: λ^W_T ≥ 2^−49162 for all 0 < T ≤ 17/16 (monotonicity, Paper 47 lem:monoT), and since λ^W_T ≤ λ^prim ≤ λ_A(T) (Paper 47 thm:A, rem:Kprim), also λ_A(T) > 0 on (0, 17/16]. 17/16 = 1.0625 > ½log5 = 0.8047; even Thm A (T = 1 > ½log 7 = 0.973) passes ½log5. **So Paper 47's "certified range up to ½log5" is superseded in range (not in constant) — label CITED (alphaXiv preprint, unrefereed, certificate not yet publicly archived).** Paper 47's own theorems (log5A/W) stay PROVED and keep much larger constants (2.5e-12, 1e-18 vs 2^−151 ≈ 3.5e-46).
Caveat: the constants 2^−151 and 2^−49162 come from a block-Schur with doubly exponential loss (consistent with Paper 47 prop:env / Zhu Thm 1.4); this is a range record, not a method toward all T. No effect on Gate/D mechanism; it changes the first-contact lower bound from ½log5 to 17/16 (CITED).

#### 4. Paper 47 sentences that become outdated (main.tex line numbers)
Rule: keep every PROVED statement; add the cited extension; do not replace ½log5 in statements proved in-paper.

(a) l.141–142 intro: "...and was certified by Zhu for $T\le0.8$ \cite[Thm.~1.2]{Zhu2026}."
→ "...was certified by Zhu for $T\le0.8$ \cite[Thm.~1.2]{Zhu2026}, and, in a preprint under review, by Liu for $T\le17/16$ with $\lamW\ge2^{-49162}$ \cite[Thm.~B]{Liu2026} (CITED; not used in any proof here)."

## IV — `AUDIT_PHASE193_CERTAINTY.md`

### Audit of certainty — every discard of phases 190–193

Question: *"we discarded many fronts — are we really sure of everything discarded?"*
Scope: `03-research/phase-193-creation-campaign/` (all CA_*_000 seed tables, CA_* memos, syntheses, adversarial reviews,
CAMPAIGN_LEDGER.md) and the phase 190–192 verdicts in this folder's README. Pen and paper; nothing re-developed.

#### 0. Strength scale and the base labels the kills rest on

Strength of a kill (weakest → strongest):
- **NUM** — rests on a NUMÉRICO datum (finite M, finite T, perturbation tests).
- **CIRC** (CIRCULAR-RISK) — the killing clause itself is ARGUED / CONDITIONAL / OPEN in Paper 47 (list below).
- **1L** (ONE-LINE) — a pre-screen sentence, no development, reviewer said only "✓".
- **ARG** (ARGUED) — written reasoning in a memo, no proof.
- **RD** (REF-D) — PROVED that the object *is* the target restated: **this is not a closure**, since a reformulation of D is
  a valid objective, attacked by its constructive tractability. An RD discard means "no progress by itself", never "impossible".
- **CIT** (PROVED-BY-CITATION) — rests on a PROVED Paper 47 lemma / falsifier (O1–O4, O6–O8, O13–O15; lem:shape-ident (B″);
  lem:shape-est (i)–(ii); thm:O; thm:sos; cor:Qp; cor:Tarch; σ_T(0)<0) whose hypotheses were checked to cover the seed.
- **THM** (PROVED-THEOREM) — a written, reviewed proof covering this exact construction.

Status of the clauses that kills invoke (grep-verified in Paper 47 main.tex, def:shape-ops l. 8328, thm:shape l. 8853,
lem:shape-* l. 8370–8527, lem:shape-est l. 8664):

| clause | status in Paper 47 | effect on kills that use it alone |
|---|---|---|
| O1, O2, O3, O4 (c large/small), O6, O7, O8, O13, O14, O15 falsifiers | PROVED | sound (CIT) |
| O4^ε, O5 | CONDITIONAL on κ_T ≠ 0 / c_{F⋆}(log n₀) ≠ 0 | CIRC |
| O10 Epstein | CITED for the complete form, ARGUED for the primitive bottom | CIRC for primitive-bottom kills |
| O11 Beurling | ARGUED (no window form of a Beurling system shown negative) | CIRC |
| O12 ζ_K | falsifier OPEN; (R)(10) is a standard-of-proof clause, not an impossibility | CIRC |
| (B′) "no estimate carries the sign" | lem:shape-est (i),(ii) PROVED, (iii) CONDITIONAL, **(iv) the reading ARGUED** | CIRC unless the seed's loss is shown > proved margin |

Seed vs idea column: **S** = kill covers the seed as formulated (a property set); a reformulation that adds a load-bearing
ζ-specific ingredient is not excluded (thm:shape(C) says every proof must contain one). **I** = kill covers the whole idea
(structural impossibility of the mechanism itself). **S/I** = mixed.

#### 2. Systematic findings

1. **REF-D is the single largest discard category (≈30 items) and it is not a closure.** Every RD verdict
   is PROVED as an equivalence, but reformulations of D are valid objectives in their own right. The campaign used "REF-D" as a
   stop. The correct label is "restatement — rank by constructive tractability". None of these was ranked by tractability.
2. **Kills resting on CIRC clauses** (O11 ARGUED, O12 OPEN, O10 primitive ARGUED, (B′)(iv) ARGUED, κ_T≠0 CONDITIONAL, H0(b)
   ARGUED, G1 via (R)(10)) account for ≈15 items. In most of them a PROVED falsifier (O2, O7, O15) or (B″) also applies, so the
   kill survives the downgrade. **The exceptions — killed by a CIRC clause alone — are J4′ (O11 only), H10/G10/G12-monoid (G1
   only), D4 Iwasawa ((R)(10)), G5 VOA (O10 primitive only), SPEC_A ((γ) used the unproved doubly-exponential scale).**
3. **The [crit] screen rests on NUMÉRICO M^{−3}.** The proved substitute (margin ≤ 4·10⁹Te^{−15.449T}, lem:shape-est(i)) supports
   every [crit] kill against perturbative/constant-loss methods, but only through the ARGUED reading (iv). The kills are very likely
   right; their label is ARG, not PROVED.
4. **Almost all O-kills are seed-level (S).** thm:shape(C) guarantees a proof must contain a property destroyed by all
   modifications; a seed killed because it survives O7 is killed *as formulated*, and the idea escapes if a load-bearing ζ-specific
   ingredient is added. Idea-level (I) kills are few and solid: commutative collapse/Schur NO-GO (E), RP false for every atomic comb,
   frustration (no ferromagnetic gauge), Markov class via O2, magic function via thm:O, free independence of commuting elements,
   Pila–Wilkie vacuity, Golden–Thompson equality, closure of the Hardy cone.
5. **Adversarial reviewers confirmed every discard**, but several confirmations are one-line "✓" on one-line kills (F6–F15, G4–G11,
   E3, E10–E12, J8, K11–K12, L7–L10). Confirmation of a one-line kill is itself one-line.
6. **Labels that drifted upward**: index README phrase "NO-GO" for Lewis–Zagier (ARGUED), condensed MW-3 generic (ARGUED; PROVED only
   for three classes), Pila–Wilkie (ARGUED in index although near-immediate), SPEC_A (rests on the retracted scale). Recommend
   re-labelling in the README (not done here: audit only).

#### 3. Discards that deserve re-examination, ranked by plausibility of an escape

1. **CA_I_001 Cor 6 — the property set 𝖯⋆ = {(S⁺), pole residue, entire with FE and Γ_ℝ, Markov ∀T}.** The only object of the
   campaign not closed under any declared single modification (O14 OPEN). Discarded as "a separation, not an inequality ⇒ REF-D as
   route" — that step is ARGUED, and thm:shape(C) says exactly that a proof must use such a property. Escape: a deduction whose
   load-bearing line is 𝖯⋆ (first: settle O14's Markov status, then ask what Markov-∀T forces on λ_A). Highest priority.
2. **CA_L_002 prime-site LP / torus certificate (L5/L6).** Attained dual, slackness set = minimizer, exact for |X| ≤ 5 — the exact
   analogue of Viazovska's structure. Killed as RD + comb-generic (true for the LP as formulated). Escape: an LP whose constraint set
   contains a ζ-specific datum (FE/pole via the archimedean column) with |X| → ∞ controlled by the elliptope rank. RD ≠ impossible.
3. **D8 amplitude-exponent homotopy W(α).** One-line ARG kill; W(α) is defined for real α without zero-freeness, and W(k) ≥ 0 at
   integers is PROVED (CA_D_001). The real question — a convexity/interpolation in α between integer data and α = 0 — was never
   examined. Seed-level kill.
4. **CA_K_002 site independence (Arch ≥ Near on prime-sited tests) and (S)/(N) restatements.** RD, but they are the most concrete
   reformulations produced (finite matrices, explicit Chen-type shifts). They should be ranked by tractability, not
   closed.
5. **CA_A_001 residue: Mellin-in-y / Rankin–Selberg in w reaching ζ(½+iτ) on the unitary axis** and **CA_A_003 §4 metaplectic
   off-diagonal packet form** — both left OPEN in the ledger, never developed; CA_A_004 Salié/Kuznetsov OPEN-RESIDUE. ⚠ [etiqueta revisada: ver Parte VII.A / Parte VI]
6. **P191 SPEC_A.** Its main kill (γ) used the unproved doubly exponential scale; the remaining kills are RD (L* exact) and (θ).
   Re-run the (γ) check with the proved margin; the RD part then becomes a tractability question.
7. **C5/F3 condensed HM with archimedean (liquid) input** — explicitly ARGUED and uncovered by CA_F_001's three classes.
8. **G7/J5 total positivity of order ≤ 4** (PF₄ OPEN) and **CA_A_007 §4 rigged-space eigenvectors built from primes** — the
   memo itself names the escape.
9. **J4′, H10, G10/G12 (monoid form), G5, D4** — killed only by CIRC clauses; escape requires naming a property separating ζ from
   Beurling/ξ_K, which these seeds as formulated cannot do; low plausibility, but the kill is not a proof.
10. **CA_A_002 Lewis–Zagier** — ARGUED; low plausibility (Λ absent), verify ψ_s formula before relying on the NO-GO label.

#### 4. Overall statement of certainty

- **Certain (PROVED, idea-level):** about 15 structural NO-GOs (commutative collapse and Schur NO-GO, RP failure, frustration,
  Markov class, thm:O magic functions, Hardy-cone closure, Hecke multiplicativity, J(1)=∞, inversion false, classical HM class,
  site arithmetic information-free, identities valid for every comb). These close mechanisms, not just seeds.
- **Certain as formulated (PROVED / CITED, seed-level):** about 35 kills through PROVED falsifiers O1–O3, O6–O8, O15 or (B″). They do
  not exclude a reformulation that adds a load-bearing ζ-specific property.
- **Not closures:** about 30 REF-D verdicts. They are PROVED restatements and remain objectives in their own right.
- **Weak (one-line, ARGUED, CIRC, NUM):** about 25 kills. Most would survive a downgrade because a PROVED falsifier also applies, but
  ≈8 rest on a CIRC clause alone or on the unproved margin scale.
- **Honest summary:** the campaign's statement "0 admissible candidates" is reliable in the narrow sense that no seed *as formulated*
  passes the PROVED filters. The stronger reading "these areas are closed" is not established: roughly one third of the discards are
  REF-D (not closures), one quarter are one-line or argued, and the single best object found (𝖯⋆) was set aside by an ARGUED step.
  No discard was found to be wrong; several are under-proved or over-labelled.

## IV — `AUDIT_ZENODO_FRONTIER.md`

### Audit : Zenodo frontier items (survey S1 B1, B2, B3, B5, B8)

Read-only, adversarial audit. Paper 47 not edited. Sources were downloaded to a scratch directory, not the repo.

#### 0. Common conventions
Every item writes Weil's form in the logarithmic variable as Q(f) = 2|∫f cosh(x/2)|² − 2|∫f sinh(x/2)|² + (1/2π)∫a(t)|F_f(t)|²dt − 2Σ_{n<e^{2L}} Λ(n)n^{-1/2} Re∫f·conj f(x−log n), with a(t) = Re ψ(1/4+it/2) − log π. Note that 2|c|² − 2|s|² = 2Re(F(i/2)·conj F(−i/2)) = 2Re(A B̄). So Q = W_T = 𝔞_T + 2Re(AB̄), the complete form with the pole term kept, on L²(I_T), with **L = T** (the support half-width). This is the same matching as Liu (AUDIT_LIU §2).
- "Width log μ" (Mori) means e^{2L} = μ, that is **T = ½ log μ**. So "width log 15" is **T = ½log15 = 1.354025** (prime powers 2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,13). The answer to the question in the brief is yes.
- Mori V and Guo use the multiplicative window [λ⁻¹,λ] on L²(du/u). This is unitarily equivalent to L²([−log λ, log λ]), so T = log λ and μ = λ² = e^{2T}.
- Ziad uses odd functions with ∫u sinh(x/2) = 0. On odd functions ∫u cosh = 0 holds automatically, so this is exactly **the odd sector of Paper 47's primitive space P_T** (both Tate moments vanish), and λ₁ is the odd-sector primitive bottom.
- Domain: C² or C_c^∞ functions are a form core of the closed form (same remark as in the Liu audit), so the bounds pass to λ^W_T.

#### B1. Mori, "Weil positivity on the window of width log 15" (zenodo 23281236; code 23092422 v1.6.2 = github moriryota/prolate-weil-bounds certificate-VIII; data 23281176)
(a) Theorem O: Q(f) ≥ 2^{-2904}‖f‖² for every complex C² function f with supp f ⊂ [−½log15, ½log15]. In our notation: **λ^W_T ≥ 2^{-2904} at T = ½log15**. By lem:monoT this holds for all T ≤ ½log15. Since λ^W ≤ λ^P ≤ λ_A, it also gives λ_A > 0 there.
Proof chain:
- bounded comparison (Liu framework plus Mori papers VII/IX, i.e. the log 10 and log 12 papers, which were not audited here);
- weighted Schur bound ‖C_p‖ ≤ 66/16;
- out-of-band tail with C = log(Ω/2π) − 1/Ω − γ and Ω = 736;
- Legendre projection with N = 1664 (832 modes per parity);
- block elimination;
- the finite matrix inequality (2.2) certified in Arb by a congruence test.
(b) Rigor and reproducibility:
- The code and 1.8 GB of data are public (Apache/CC-BY), with SHA-pinned sources.
- Checker and proposer are separate programs, and there is an independent re-check. Seven mutation tests were rejected.
- AI-generated (Claude/GPT), not refereed, not formalized.

**My independent recomputation (mpmath, no shared code):**
- c = ΩL = 996.5625
- −log₂ d(c) = 2900.286
- C = 0.1369944
- u₀E₀ = 0.136844 < C and u₁E₁ = 0.136341 < C
- Cδ ≥ 2^{-2904} holds
- max R_w on a 2·10⁵-point grid = 4.09133 ≤ 66/16 = 4.125 (paper: 4.0915 on 2304 Arb cells)

The author's scalars.py also passes (log₂(α+βb²) = −697.74 < −697).

Gap: the shipped independent_scalars.py fails because notes/0792_claude_lowmem_generator/scalar_mu15.json is missing from the release. This is minor.

**§B1-run (done , scratchpad).**
- Code: github v1.6.2 certificate-VIII.
- Data: 46 files fetched from github raw; all SHA-256 sums match; restore.py reports "all 24 data files restored and verified".
- Ran `check_certificate.py --bits 1280` (python-flint 0.9.0) in 283 s, 3.5 GB. Result: **PASS_EXTERNAL_CERTIFICATE**.
- λ_min(T) ≥ 2.3979369226737e−70 (even) and 3.9458005898258e−66 (odd), with ε_T = 4.79e−94. These are exactly the paper's Table 2.
- Independent entry check: A₀₀ (even) = γ − ⟨v₀, C_p v₀⟩ = 37/8 − Σ_{n<15} Λ(n)n^{-1/2}·2(2L−log n)/(2L) = 1.3127070815421376549595321292 by my own mpmath. It agrees with the packet's dyadic centre to 40 digits. This confirms the prime set (including 13) and the normalization.
- Not done: regenerating J (7800 s/parity); the analytic lemmas of papers VII/IX.

(c) Consistency with our data:
- Fuchs: 1−λ₄(c) ≈ (4√π 8⁴/4!) c^{9/2} e^{-2c}, with c = 2πμ.
- At μ = 15 this gives about 1.5e−70. Times Mori's Galerkin ratio of 4–5, that is about 7e−70.
- The certified finite margin is 2.40e−70 (even), the lowest eigenvalue of a Schur complement of M+V, which must be ≥ λ_min of the compressed form. **The orders of magnitude match.**
- The certificate does resolve levels about 10⁻⁷⁰. It does so with 3328-bit arithmetic, and all paid errors are < 2^{-300} ≈ 5e−91.
- The final constant 2^{-2904} ≈ 10^{-874} is the out-of-band δ ~ e^{-2ΩL}. It sits far below the true bottom, so there is no tension.
- Our NUMÉRICO μ_even ≤ 2.5e−22 at T = 1 (BARRIER_Z_001, M = 64, not converged and still decreasing with M) is an upper bound. It is consistent with the Fuchs-model value of about 9e−30 at μ = e². Our Galerkin data simply do not resolve the bottom at T ≥ 1. This needs no correction, but it should be recorded: **the true bottom at T = 1 is plausibly ~1e−29**.
- **Margin plausible.**

Verdict: **VERIFIED (computational part)**. The certificate was reproduced, and the scalars and the A entry were checked independently. The analytic reduction of papers VII/IX (Prop 3.1, Lemma 3.2, block elimination) was not re-proved here. Label for Paper 47/index: **CITED** (unrefereed, AI-generated, but externally reproducible). λ^W_T ≥ 2^{-2904} for T ≤ ½log15.

#### B2. Mori, "Improved upper bounds for windowed Weil forms with exponential factor e^{-4πμ}" (zenodo 23363767, v3; concept 23175060)
(a) Theorem K, unconditional. With λ_min = λ^W_T and T = ½log μ:
- λ_min ≤ 3.50e24 μ^{9/2} log μ e^{-4πμ} for 50 ≤ μ ≤ 10⁴;
- λ_min ≤ 7.58e24 μ⁵(log μ)³ e^{-4πμ} for all μ ≥ 50.
Method: an explicit smoothed prolate test vector, with the zero sum bounded using RH verified up to 3·10¹² and a zero-free region. These are upper bounds only. Conjecture 1.2 is λ_min ≍ μ^{9/2}e^{-4πμ}. The earlier bound from the same series is 1.362e9 λ^{46} e^{-4πλ²} for μ ≥ 5 (cited by Guo).

(d) Comparison with ours. cor:margin1 is λ_A ≤ 4e9·T·e^{-15.449T}, which is **singly** exponential in T. Mori's bound is **doubly** exponential: exp(−4πe^{2T}).

| T | cor:margin1 | Mori 1.362e9 μ^{23}e^{-4πμ} (μ ≥ 5) | Mori Thm K value (proved only for μ ≥ 50) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 781 (vacuous) | 6e−12 | (2.7e−12) |
| ½log15 | 4.5 (vacuous) | 2e−46 | (2.6e−52) |
| 1.956 (μ = 50) | 5.9e−4 | 2e−225 | 8e−241 |
| 2.5 | 1.7e−7 | 1e−751 | 1e−775 |

cor:margin1 bounds λ_A, while Mori bounds λ^W ≤ λ_A, so the two are not directly comparable. Mori uses zero data (verified RH up to a height and a zero-free region); Paper 47 cor:margin1 removes one zero via the testfam family. Even so, as a ceiling on certificate methods **Mori's bound is overwhelmingly stronger** for λ^W, and it supersedes the "e^{-15.449T}" scale as the quantitative barrier for any complete-form certificate. prop:env (τ_env doubly exponential in T) is consistent with this: both say the resolution needed grows like exp(e^{2T}).

Verdict: **PLAUSIBLE-UNVERIFIED**. The proof was not checked line by line; the bound is consistent with the B1 margin and with the Fuchs asymptotics. Recommended label: CITED.

#### B3. Guo Chen, "Prolate leakage and near-zero spectral clusters…" (zenodo 23297284)
(a) Theorem 1.1: for λ ≥ Λ_m, A_λ has ≥ m eigenvalues in [−δ_m, δ_m], δ_m ≲ λ^{4m+17/2}e^{-πλ²}, via the summation map E applied to prolates with f(0) = f̂(0) = 0. This is an exact residual identity (Thm 4.5) plus transfer and nondegeneracy.
The constants are astronomical: log Λ_m ≤ 700(4m+5)⁴. Theorem 1.8 (m = 1) needs λ ≥ 2^{15}/√(2π) for part (b), and λ ≥ 232 (T ≥ 5.4) for parts (d) and (e).
**This is vacuous at every window we work at (T ≤ 2).** Its value is structural: an unconditional NO-GO quantifier saying the near-kernel has growing multiplicity. Any lower-bound method must separate m clustered eigenvalues at scale e^{-πμ}. It is the multiplicity version of the CCM mechanism (L06/L39).

Verdict: **PLAUSIBLE-UNVERIFIED** (classical ingredients; not checked line by line). Record in the index as a NO-GO quantifier, not as a route.

#### B5. Senke, window (−77/64, 77/64) (zenodo 22871384, v0.3)
The record is **Restricted**: no files are public. Only the description is available. It describes a cellwise Schur certificate plus a Binet tail plus a dyadic transfer, with prime powers 2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11 and T = 1.203125.
Nothing can be checked. The window is also superseded in range by Mori ½log12 = 1.242 and ½log15 = 1.354.

Verdict: **UNVERIFIABLE (restricted)**. This is treated as PLAUSIBLE-UNVERIFIED at most. Do not cite.

#### B8. Ziad, "Localized constrained Weil forms: near-degeneracy and a Davenport–Heilbronn first kernel" (zenodo 23145455)
(a) Zeta, odd primitive sector at T = ½log7: 0 < λ₁ < 5.0023e−19.
- The upper bound comes from an 80-mode Legendre witness: archimedean 0.2157094617577142245 against prime −0.2157094617577142240. Arb, ±3.8e−51.
- The lower bound comes from a 431-mode head plus an analytic tail (Schur).
- The coefficients are not published; the record contains only the PDF, and "no separate Git repository".
- The result is consistent with our μ_odd (3.8e−18 to 5.3e−20 at T = 1, not converged).

(e) DH witness: the form for F = Σa_n n^{-s} with a_n periodic mod 5 (0, 1, κ, −κ, −1), gamma factor Γ((s+1)/2)(5/π)^{(s+1)/2}, α = 3/4, coefficients b_n/√n from −F′/F. These coefficients are real but **not supported on prime powers** (for example b₆ = (1+κ²)log6 ≠ 0), and **there is no Euler product and no pole**.
- The constraint ⊥ sinh(x/2) is imposed artificially.
- Positivity holds for a ≤ ½log2: no shifts, and an analytic floor of 0.4289.
- The negative witness at a = 9/5: 140 sine modes, Rayleigh quotient −6.1690e−9 ± 4e−23 (archimedean 2.38352025058 against arithmetic up to n ≤ 36, −2.38352025675).
- **Admissibility:** the witness is exactly constrained, odd and supported in (−9/5, 9/5), so as a test function it lies in the odd part of our P_T with T = 9/5. But the form is **not** our W_T: archimedean kernel K_{3/4}, conductor 5, and non-prime-power coefficients. It is therefore a falsifier only for method classes that use nothing beyond the functional equation, a gamma factor and a Dirichlet series (no multiplicativity of the coefficients, no Euler product). It is not a datum about W_T.
- Its window 9/5 = 1.8 lies well beyond our working windows. The first-loss scale is bracketed only loosely: (½log2, 9/5).
- Plausibility: DH's first off-line zero is near 0.808 + 85.7i. The witness bandwidth is 140π/1.8 ≈ 244, enough to reach it. A 9-digit cancellation is of the kind expected near a first crossing. The result is plausible.

Verdict: **PLAUSIBLE-UNVERIFIED** (not reproducible: coefficients and code are absent). Use: add to the index as falsifier test **F-DH**: "any proposed carrier/certificate method that does not use the Euler product must fail for DH at some a < 9/5". This complements the Beurling and cΛ falsifiers. This is consistent with the semiring principle (the sign must come from the (ℕ,+,·) structure).

#### Index actions
- B1: record the frontier datum (CITED pending human review). The certified first-contact lower bound moves from 17/16 (Liu) to ½log15 = 1.354. Route class: dual certificate / bounded comparison (KNOWN; no new mechanism for all T).
- B2: record the doubly exponential ceiling exp(−4πe^{2T}) as the quantitative barrier for complete-form certificates.
- B3: record as a NO-GO quantifier (multiplicity of the near-kernel).
- B5: UNVERIFIABLE, superseded.
- B8: record falsifier F-DH, with the caveat that its form is not W_T.

# Parte VI — Verificación contra los memos originales

Resultado de cotejar el índice con los memos originales, tramo por tramo. Cada tramo lista: cobertura; rutas
ausentes del índice; resultados positivos ausentes; discrepancias de etiqueta entre el memo y el índice; y la
lista de archivos ya cubiertos. **Donde esta Parte contradice a las Partes I–IV, manda esta Parte**: las
etiquetas de las Partes I–IV provienen de índices anteriores y no de los memos. Los números de línea «l.NNN»
citados en los tramos son los de este archivo en el momento del cotejo y se desplazan al crecer el archivo:
búsquese por identificador.

Método: de cada archivo del tramo se leyó el texto completo si tiene hasta 70 líneas; si es más largo, las
primeras 28 líneas, las últimas 14 y todas las líneas intermedias con veredictos, etiquetas o enunciados; el
original se abrió cuando eso no bastaba. Lo no leído de los memos largos queda sin cotejar.

#### §2 RUTAS AUSENTES (c)

##### phase-162 — Unicidad del residuo Gamma del modo homogéneo (mecanismo B2)
- Archivos: R162_102_B2_GAMMA_RESIDUE_UNIQUENESS.md
- Qué se intentó: obtener el cierre de la puerta 1 por unicidad del modo homogéneo del defecto W⁰_ε (R161_017/019/025), separando (H-germ) «W⁰_ε≡0» de (H-int) «restricción interior nula».
- Resultado según el memo: «NO-GO (as an independent closing mechanism)». Prop 1.1 PROVED (unicidad a nivel germen, trivial y sin Euler; equivale a la puerta 1); Prop 2.1 PROVED módulo hechos estándar: en el modelo Davenport–Heilbronn existe un modo homogéneo interior no nulo (unicidad (H-int) FALSA allí); Prop 3.1 PROVED (estructural: la cadena B2 no usa producto de Euler). (H-int) para el objeto aritmético: OPEN, más débil que la puerta 1.
- Por qué falla: falla F3 en sentido fuerte; Λ∗1=log sólo podría entrar por el paso no probado (PC)→dispersión (L161.8).
- Reapertura escrita: un argumento (H-int) futuro debe usar el espacio polo/Tate o el producto de Euler en el paso que fuerza la anulación; el modelo DH es el falsificador.
- Lo más cercano en el índice: nada con el identificador. R161_019/024-025 (l.5072, 12328) para la rigidez de polos; F-DH (l.4426) no lista 102. La fila G2B-R162_103 (l.5235) es otro mecanismo (B3).

##### phase-162 — Residuo de R162_1201: positividad de Stieltjes/Kreĭn del núcleo κ frente al peine
- Archivos: R162_1201_SONIN_RANGE.md §6
- Qué se dejó: «A closing argument must use the inequality H ≥ 0 together with (S): e.g. a Kreĭn-type statement that the Jordan chain {e^{a_m t},(T−t)e^{a_m t}} … cannot become neutral … Candidate input: the Stieltjes positivity of κ (κ is completely monotone …, Kreĭn string theory) against the comb — not attempted here».
- Resultado según el memo: la ruta del rango de Sonin es NO-GO (PROVED); el residuo es una propuesta no intentada.
- Lo más cercano en el índice: G1B-R162_1201 (l.5142, 12360) «rango de Sonin ⟺ HF=0, Müntz todo-o-nada», sin el residuo; nada sobre «completamente monótono»/«cuerda de Kreĭn» vinculado a 1201 (la única coincidencia, l.3674, es R155_044/045, otro objeto).

#### §3 RESULTADOS POSITIVOS AUSENTES (d)

##### phase-161 — Lema de detección finita en el radical
- Archivo: R161_046 (y uso en R161_071, R161_073)
- Enunciado: para T fijo y N subespacio de dimensión finita de L²(−T,T), la cadena N∩ker ℓ_1∩…∩ker ℓ_M (ℓ_m(F)=∫F e^{−a_m t}, a_m=2m+½) se estabiliza en {0} tras finitos pasos; por tanto finitos momentos de polos Gamma detectan el radical de primer contacto. Etiqueta: «proved, using imported compact resolvent and moment completeness».
- Índice: sólo como título de la fila G8B-R161_046-051 (l.5228, 12352), clase DEAD; el lema como herramienta no figura (R161_073–074 OPEN-RESIDUE, l.4960, lo presupone). No retractado.

##### phase-161 — Collar exponencial exacto bajo traslación finita
- Archivo: R161_047 (y R161_048)
- Enunciado: ℓ_a(P τ_h F)=e^{ah}[ℓ_a(F)−L_{a,h}(F)]; para S_N, ℓ_a(PS_NF)=Σ_{n≤min(N,e^{2T})} n^{a−½}[ℓ_a(F)−L_{a,log n}(F)]; residuo de la parte exterior = K_F(a_m). R161_048: estabilización interior exacta P_T Z_N F = P_T S_N F para N≥e^{2T}. Etiqueta: «formulas (1)-(3) proved».
- Índice: no nombrados (cubiertos sólo por la fila DEAD 046-051). No retractados.

#### §2 RUTAS AUSENTES (c)

##### phase-162 — Inserción literal del defecto de Ward en la identidad de Green de cuatro bloques
- Archivos: R162_205
- Qué se intentó: insertar el defecto divisorial b_a = a*1 − log de una modificación finita a = Λ+η (R162_204) en los pares de Green mixtos / doble conmutador de R161_057–060, esperando un cuadrado del jet crítico.
- Resultado según el memo: «EXACT NO-GO FOR LITERAL GREEN SUBSTITUTION / GATE 1 OPEN»; contribución de Ward finita a (PC) y defecto interior Δ_N^a (1.2)–(1.3) PROVED; su contribución de Green es impar e indefinida PROVED; producción de cuadrado de jet REJECTED.
- Por qué falló: el término de defecto es lineal, cambia de signo con η→−η y se anula en a=Λ; lo que queda en a=Λ es la correlación exterior no resuelta de R161_057–060.
- Reapertura: ley de conservación independiente de segundo parámetro o de diferencia coherente (OPEN).
- Lo más cercano: l.5017 (G1C-R161_057-060, «sustitución literal PC», REF-D); l.4990 / l.12359 (G1B-R162_204). Ninguna fila nombra R162_205.

- Archivos: R162_302 (auditoría R162_390)

Lemma 1.1 (superdiferencial = envolvente convexa de −c_F|_{log N_T}, F∈K_*), Lemma 4.1 (‖R_LF‖² = ε⟨c_F,κ_L⟩) y Prop 5.1 (A)+(B) ⟹ Gate 1 PROVED; (i) y (iii) NO-GO (átomo entrante invisible a primer orden; direcciones Ward-preservantes vacías, Lemma 3.1; exteriores estacionarias y silenciosas, Lemma 3.2). Auditoría 390: CORRECT WITH FIXES; «(5.1) ⟺ (A)» y «(B) no contiene Λ» erróneos.
- Por qué falló: (i) pasa F3 (thm:finmod); (iii) vacía; (ii) se cierra en R162_304.
- Reapertura: sub-lema C2.1 (Ward exterior), cerrado NO-GO en R162_305 (que sí está, l.5021).
- Lo más cercano: l.5021 (G1B-R162_305). R162_302 no aparece.

##### phase-162 — Construcción de la dirección α (D1) de la Prop 5.1 de R162_302
- Archivos: R162_304
- Qué se intentó: construir α ∈ Tan(v⁰) y β que satisfagan (A) y (B).

(B) no es arquimediana (Thm 2: sin solución para β≥0; Thm 3 reducción de Schur para β<0, depende de Λ vía K_*); (A)∧(B) sobre K_*^ε ⟺ K_*^ε = {0} (Thm 4); todo α de prueba colisiona (§4); ningún α≠0 admite certificado direccional global (Thm 5).

#### §2 RUTAS AUSENTES (c)

##### phase-163 — Redondeo aleatorio de Witt: contramodelos discretos hasta θ=1/3
- Archivos: R163_103, R163_105 (auditoría interna), R163_110 (auditoría lógica del umbral BF)
- Qué se intentó: redondeo independiente de los coeficientes de Witt w_{p,m} del sistema extendido Z_θ(s)=ζ((s−θ)/(1−θ)), con lema de momentos que controla todos los órdenes del producto de convolución.
- Resultado según el memo: 103 «complete internal proof, pending external review»: para 1/3<θ<1/2 existe sistema discreto con N=ρx+O_ε(x^{θ+ε}) y ceros en Re s=(1+θ)/2; 105: sin hueco lógico, pide revisión externa; 110: la conclusión BF aplicada sólo a ζ da [H] únicamente si 0<θ₀≤1/2 (corrección al Problema 6 del Paper 48); con 103, el rango posible queda 0<θ₀≤1/3.
- Por qué falló o qué cierra: refuta la meta de clase BF para 1/3<θ₀<3/4; no da ley para ζ; no resuelve θ<1/3 ni θ=0.
- Reapertura: «another mechanism: one that uses ζ's exact arithmetic and does not extend to these discrete systems».
- Lo más cercano en el índice: G5G-R163_803 Theorem C (l.5483, l.12480) «Novedad: chequeo Diamond–Zhang pendiente»; no registra el método ni la corrección de umbral de 110 (0<θ₀≤1/2 vs «cualquier θ₀>0»).

##### phase-163 — Transporte de primos emparejados y referencia Q(i)
- Archivos: R163_104
- Qué se intentó: criterio T_{σ₀}(P,Q)=Σ|log(q_j/p_j)|min^{−σ₀}<∞ ⟹ ζ_Q/ζ_P holomorfa sin ceros en Re s>σ₀; Q(i) con N=(π/4)x+O(x^{131/416}).
- Resultado: teorema de transporte PROVED; Q(i) CITED (Huxley); condición necesaria falsable.
- Por qué no cierra: un umbral BF θ₀=1/3 incluiría Q(i) e implicaría además el análogo para L(s,χ_{−4}); se recomienda buscar una ley de retículo exacto orientado.
- Lo más cercano: nada (Q(i)/131/416 sin coincidencias).

##### phase-163 — Cociclo entrópico ×p de Φ_Λ y su acoplamiento al contacto
- Archivos: R163_106, R163_107, R163_131
- Qué se intentó: E_p(h)=⟨Φ_Λ,e^{h(p·)}−e^h⟩=(log p)[e^{h(0)}−∫e^h]; signo coercivo de Jensen en la sección h(0)=∫h; levantamiento canónico de Möbius h_F.
- Resultado: 106 identidad y cota PROVED, acoplamiento OPEN; 107 NO-GO: h_F(0)−∫h_F=2‖F‖² para todo F (defecto independiente del contacto); 131 PROVED: con el lift cruzado el primer signo es cuártico, −(log p)r⁴‖b_F‖²/2; un puente cuadrático puro es incompatible por escala.
- Reapertura (107): un h_{F,s} con perfil meromorfo y correcciones Gamma/exteriores; (131) no excluye puente cuártico, pero R162_903 Thm 5.1 lo reduce a cuadrático tensorial.
- Lo más cercano: nada propio (búsqueda «entrop»: sólo clasificadores y Λ=μ∗log entropía ×p de 6B en el grid).

##### phase-163 — Intercambio infinito atómico y obstrucciones de un primo, finitos primos y capacidad local
- Archivos: R163_108, R163_109, R163_111, R163_112
- Qué se intentó: modelo E_δ=1+sinh²(aδ)/cosh²(aw) con corriente atómica en k log 2; exclusión de intercambios periódicos de un primo (polo bajo π/log p), de productos periódicos sobre finitos primos (densidad de Ingham), y capacidad 1/k para factores racionales locales.
- Resultado: los cuatro PROVED bajo sus hipótesis; ninguno excluye corrientes multiprimo no periódicas; 113 los reclasifica como pruebas adversariales.
- Lo más cercano: G5F-R163_002a (l.5457) sólo para el caso finito; nada para 108–112.

##### phase-163 — Colapso tipo Hamburger: soporte de Euler, soporte en log ℕ, cociente discreto con primer hueco
- Archivos: R163_113, R163_114, R163_126
- Qué se intentó: si log E^{-1} tiene serie de Euler ordinaria (113), si supp q_E ⊂ log ℕ_{≥2} (114), o si ζ/E es serie de Dirichlet generalizada con primer hueco a>0 (126), entonces E≡1.
- Resultado: reducciones condicionales PROVED; la hipótesis no se deriva de la aritmética («full strength of [H]»).
- Por qué no cierra: la hipótesis de soporte/representación es el problema entero.
- Lo más cercano: Hamburger aparece en el índice (p. ej. W3′ R163_1001, l.3968; G5F-R163_1001b, l.5325) pero no estas tres reducciones; R163_1001 lista 113/114 como «DEAD routes read», sin fila propia en el índice.

- Resultado: todos PROVED como lemas (116 usa la cota de 115; 125 usa la verificación hasta 3·10¹²); la puerta (obtener el hueco de q_E desde (PC-ren)/Poisson–Tate) OPEN; 123 «not a NO-GO for every possible construction».
- Reapertura escrita: término orientado y firmado que transporte información del cono de cuadrados al test H_b (123); comparación M₃≤(b+η)M₂, η<0.24, desde input aritmético independiente (125).

#### §2 RUTAS AUSENTES (c)

##### phase-163 — Inclinación de Euler del mismo peso (cociente Z_a(z+u)/Z_a(z))
- Archivos: R163_144
- Qué se intentó: familia r_{a,u}=μ_a∗(b_a·(·)^{−u}); derivadas r'=−a, r''=W_a=a·log+a∗a; varianza positiva en los puntos Gamma s_m=2m+1; transferir el signo al núcleo físico.
- Resultado según el memo: «exact deformation family and curvature computation… The positive result lives at the Gamma points; its pullback to the physical kernel remains open. Does not close Row D.»
- Por qué falla: la positividad (4)–(6) es escalar para x>1; el objeto físico es el emparejamiento cruzado F/A_aF; los modelos κ satisfacen la misma positividad y tienen contacto.
- Reapertura: usar la coincidencia retículo–Euler de R163_143 dentro de una identidad Poisson–Tate orientada y de compresión.
- Lo más cercano en el índice: nada.

##### phase-163 — Rectángulo Euler–Poisson de la inclinación y falsificador Z_c
- Archivos: R163_145
- Qué se intentó: T(s,u)=ζ(s+u)/ζ(s) = Γ(s,u)·T(1−s,−u); acoplar con los dos puertos de 143 y la inclinación de 144.
- Resultado: identidades meromorfas exactas + falsificador calculado; «no transfer of positivity to the compression, Row D remains open». En la recta, la ecuación fija Re L pero no Re W. Falsificador `Z_c(s)=ζ(s)exp(c(s−1/2)²)`: misma reflexión, curvatura en 1/2 desplazada en 2c (signo arbitrario).
- Por qué falla: todo argumento basado sólo en la ecuación funcional queda refutado por Z_c; la pieza de signo debe venir del acoplamiento físico-aritmético adicional.
- Lo más cercano: nada (Z_c no figura en la batería l.4442–4447).

##### phase-163 — Métrica producto sin división ∫|ζ(½+iτ)|²|F̂|² como condición de contacto
- Archivos: R163_146
- Resultado: «direct proof of strict positivity… limited NO-GO against using its vanishing as a first-contact condition». 0<M(F)<∞; H_TF=0 no puede implicar M(F)=0. Vale también para Z_{a_κ}, Epstein/DH.
- Reapertura: diferencia orientada antes del producto, o sustracción con términos Tate/exterior que se anule selectivamente.
- Lo más cercano: G4D-R162_2502a «comparación fiel sin división» (l.5315, l.12397) — objeto distinto.

##### phase-163 — Falsificador entero de Euler por duplicación Z_K=ζ·(1−2^{−s})^{−K}
- Archivos: R163_147 (usado en 149–160, 202, 203, 290)
- Resultado: «explicit construction proved. It refutes any step using only positive Euler + integer multiplicities (without requiring b(n)≡1 and the Poisson–Tate orientation)»; contacto primero en ½log2<T_*^K<½log3.
- Por qué cierra: conserva soporte entero, multiplicidades enteras positivas, producto de Euler genuino, pesos a_K≥0 y parte Gamma de ζ, y aun así tiene contacto.
- Lo más cercano: «Z_K keeps 2-modes» dentro de G5D-R163_201b (l.12464); **no hay fila F-Z_K en la batería de falsificadores (l.4442–4447)**.

##### phase-163 — Grafo móvil de (PC-ren): colisiones de cociente, fibras de potencias primas
- Archivos: R163_148, R163_149
- Resultado: 148 Thm 1 (núcleo exacto μ_{M,N}, átomo diagonal Σ_{n≤min(M,N)}Λ(n)/n), Thm 2 (estabilización local sin uniformidad), Cor (el conmutador de dilatación pierde la diagonal) — PROVED; el átomo aislado no distingue ζ de los modelos κ. 149: clasificación exacta por cocientes reducidos (sólo denominadores potencia prima), límite c_∞(a/p^j), inversión a(p^j)=B_{p,j}−p^{−1}B_{p,j+1}; «does not resolve the gate… Row D remains open».

- Lo más cercano: G4C-R181 «peine de colisiones de cocientes» (l.3249, l.12579), objeto distinto (polarización compleja).

#### §2 RUTAS AUSENTES (c)

##### phase-155 — Decaimiento del minimizador primal (L1): perfil de borde logarítmico vía teoría de log-laplaciano
- Archivos: R155_001 §1–§2, R155_002 ítems 1–6, R155_003 §1
- Qué se intentó: tasa de decaimiento de |F̂⋆|² desde Theorem W, con la pista «Bombieri 2000 Lemma 2 ⇒ Hölder-½».
- Resultado según el memo: pista Bombieri WITHDRAWN (es Morrey para W₀^{1,2}); perfil |log(T−|t|)|^{−1/2} y μ⋆(|τ|>R) ≍ R^{−1}(log R)^{−1} CONDITIONAL (Chen–Weth/loglap, requiere principio del máximo, que es él mismo una afirmación de positividad); sólo PROVED la cola de Chebyshev μ⋆(|τ|≥R) ≤ (λ+B)/(m(R)−C₀) y la reducción a conjunto acotado sin tasa (Thm 3.3, versión λ^A).
- Por qué falló: tasa sólo condicional; R155_004 §8: «Do not reopen L1».

#### §2 RUTAS AUSENTES (c)

##### fase 159 / G1_B3_R2 — mecanismo de Iwasawa (conjetura principal) como fuente de positividad previa
- Archivos: G1_B3_R2.md (Theorem I, Props I1–I2, Cor I′, Lemma S′, Prop C_δ, Prop AP); retira W1 de G1_B3_R1.
- Qué se intentó: la positividad previa de la escuela p-ádica: retículo `Z_p` invariante de Iwasawa, actuando por un grupo compacto; prueba de si el flujo de escala de Q puede actuar por algún grupo compacto. Además la cohomología Weil–Arakelov de Flach–Morin.
- Resultado según el memo: «Dead end for the object on this angle». Theorem I PROVED (dado CITED): la positividad de Iwasawa es compacidad, controla sólo valores absolutos p-ádicos; forzar el flujo por un grupo compacto da acotación de Sz.-Nagy + casi periodicidad, de fuerza [H]. Prop WA PROVED condicional a Conj. 2.3/4.1 de Flach–Morin. Lemma S′ (tope de multiplicidad agudo, corrige Rem 2.2 de R1). Prop C_δ: problema de completitud nombrado como equivalente.
- Por qué falló: el flujo `R_{>0}` de Q es aniquilado por todo grupo aritmético compacto; la ruta de compacidad es de fuerza [H].
- Reapertura: un portador con grupo amenable no compacto (cláusula «weakest step», `HEURISTIC`/abierta).
- Lo más cercano en IDX: l.5115 «Polarizaciones Hodge/twistor/Fargues–Fontaine/condensadas | G8H-R160_S5 §2.3#21 G1_B3_R2/R3 | DEAD [muro de peso entero] | … Weil–Arakelov ciego» (no nombra Iwasawa ni Theorem I); «Iwasawa» en IDX sólo aparece por CA_C_004 (l.5853, otra ruta: racionalidad de ζ(2k)/π^{2k}).

##### fase 159 / G1_B3_R3 — anillo de Habiro con operaciones de Adams y clase producto de Fargues–Fontaine
- Archivos: G1_B3_R3.md (Theorem F, Prop H, Prop D).
- Qué se intentó: (i) la clase producto Fargues–Fontaine como portador; (ii) el anillo de Habiro con `q ↦ q^p` (escuela de Scholze, 0 citas en el corpus) como familia de Frobenius.
- Resultado según el memo: Theorem F PROVED (exclusión PROVED dado Cor H de G1_B2_R3): la clase producto FF es Euler-factorizable y cae bajo el muro de cola; excluida incondicionalmente (Hardy). Prop H PROVED en el modelo monomial: Habiro es una familia de desplazamientos tipo Bost–Connes con parte unitaria trivial. Prop D (las dos fuentes, compacidad y pesos algebraicos, agotan la positividad derivada) `HEURISTIC` como completitud.
- Por qué falló: muro de peso entero (Theorem W) y muro de cola; Habiro sin parte unitaria.
- Reapertura escrita: «reopen only with a» tercer mecanismo de positividad (Prop D heurística); Prop W4(b) (fibrado de Hilbert de rango infinito en `P¹_tw`) `OPEN`.
- Lo más cercano en IDX: l.5115 (cita G1_B3_R2/R3 por el muro de peso entero). «Habiro» 0 coincidencias; Theorem F de B3_R3 sólo indirectamente vía l.4785 (que se refiere a B3_R4–R5).

##### fase 159 / G1_B7_R1–R2 — positividad por reciprocidad tipo Ancona (fuente S4 de la conjetura estándar de tipo Hodge)
- Archivos: G1_B7_R1.md (Lemmas M3, M4, M4′, M5; tabla S1–S8), G1_B7_R2.md (Theorem B, Theorem Q1, Prop N, Cor R, Prop X, Theorem L).
- Qué se intentó: transportar la única prueba incondicional nueva de la conjetura estándar de tipo Hodge (Ancona 2021: reciprocidad de símbolos de Hilbert, piezas CM de rango chico, períodos p-ádicos) al motivo numérico `𝔐_Z`, y cerrar el «loophole de la matriz de períodos».
- Resultado según el memo: R1 «proved exclusion of the one positivity mechanism the record had not examined (M3 + M4 + M5)»; R2 «The loophole is closed. Its three branches each end in a proved obstruction or a proved circularity (Theorem L)»; Theorem B PROVED vía Baker: los números de Lefschetz atómicos `Λ(n)/√n` de la ventana T generan un `Q̄`-módulo de rango exactamente `π(e^{2T})`; recomendación: «M1 as EQUIVALENT and S4 as EXCLUDED». Lemma M4 PROVED (Jensen + Conrey): ningún test no nulo en `𝒜` ve sólo finitos ceros. Lemma M5 (Gelfond–Schneider): no hay estructura Q en los `Λ(n)/√n`.
- Por qué falló: rango de períodos infinito (Baker); estructuras racionales no compatibles son libres (Hasse–Minkowski); la rama de completaciones es circular (Theorem L(b), circularidad, no imposibilidad).
- Reapertura: (R4) suministrado por algo que no sea forma racional ni completación (memo, «Completeness of the source list»).
- Lo más cercano en IDX: l.4641 «Motivo numérico M_Z, muro de contracción | G7H-159 G1_B7 | REF-D …» (sin Ancona, Theorem B ni Theorem L); «Ancona» 0 coincidencias; «Baker» aparece sólo en otros contextos.

#### §3 RESULTADOS POSITIVOS AUSENTES (d)

##### G1_B9_R5 — O-37 de P46 cerrado en todo género (Theorem G)
- Enunciado: para `C/F_q` de género `g ≥ 1`, `|y_D| ≤ ½ deg D` para todo D efectivo en `C×C`; `σ_θ(Eff‾(C×C) ∩ V_C) = ½` en todo género; las clases que cierran la brecha `s_C → 1` son los pull-backs del divisor theta de la jacobiana por `(x,y) ↦ a·x − b·y`. #### §2 RUTAS AUSENTES (c)

##### phase-159 / G2_B1 — Parte estructurada aritmética de Green–Tao (modelo W-trick y corrección de Siegel)
- Archivos: G2_B1_R3.md.
- Qué se intentó: tomar como parte estructurada del peine el modelo periódico `s_W` del W-trick, con la corrección
  de Siegel, y escribir la escisión exacta `Λ = s_W + r_W`.
- Resultado según el memo: DEAD END, EXCLUDED. Thm G (PROVED) dice que `s_W` es una compleción de tipo ζ, rígida por
  el Thm R de R2, y que nunca reproduce el peine de la ventana. Prop Z (PROVED) dice que el polo queda del lado
  estructurado y toda la medida de ceros, con el polo cancelado, del lado pseudoaleatorio. Prop E dice que todo uso de
  la uniformidad de Gowers es una estimación excluida por thm:margin y O3. Cor Z1(a): para `s_1 ≡ 1` el centro vale −0.45.
- Por qué falló: las dos nociones de estructura disponibles (ζ × molificador y modelos periódicos) son compleciones
  de tipo ζ. Además F2 (R1 Prop 4 + thm:margin), O3 y F4 (Prop E(iii)).
- Reapertura: ninguna. Según el memo, «no remaining structured class».
- Lo más cercano en IDX: l.4762 / l.11994 (G4A-159 G2_B1). Esa fila nombra la parte estructurada de Selberg y la
  Prop P, pero no el modelo de Green–Tao, el W-trick ni la Prop Z. Un grep de «Green», «W-trick» y «Siegel model» no
  da coincidencias en este sentido.

##### phase-159 / G2_B10 — La puerta de la ecuación funcional en el método de Levinson
- Archivos: G2_B10_R2.md.
- Qué se intentó: acoplar el molificador a la ecuación funcional, como hace Levinson: molificadores simétricos
  `M(s)+M(1−s)`, la combinación diferencial `ζ + λζ′` y traslaciones por `log n`.
- Resultado según el memo: dead_end como mecanismo.
  - Prop L1 (PROVED): cada operación de Levinson actúa como restricción de la misma forma de ventana a un subespacio,
    o como combinación positiva de copias de ella. Nunca agrega positividad.
  - La parte exacta (100 %) que carga la ecuación funcional es Speiser / Levinson–Montgomery, EQUIVALENT.
  - Thm D: tabla de dicotomía detección/Weil.
- Por qué falló: la ecuación funcional sólo entra a través de restatements EQUIVALENT. Hay además un falsificador
  explícito, `L_2`.
- Reapertura: ninguna.
- Lo más cercano en IDX: l.4760 / l.11992 «Molificadores: Levinson–Conrey, Jensen, Thm Γ_f, Thm H | DEAD». No menciona
  la puerta de la ecuación funcional, Prop L1 ni Speiser. l.5010 dice «mollification = ensanchar la ventana», que
  corresponde a R3.

##### phase-159 / G2_B1 — Teoremas probados del ángulo estructura/aleatoriedad (R1, R2, R4, R5)
- Archivos: G2_B1_R1, R2, R4, R5.
- Enunciados:
  - R1, Prop 1 (PROVED): toda compleción libre de ceros da una representación exacta de la forma de ventana sin ceros.
    Cor 1: una nueva clase de puntos duales.
  - R2, Thm R (rigidez, PROVED): toda compleción `ζ·P` que reproduce el peine está forzada a la familia de Selberg
    `b_d = μ(d)(α − log d)`. Lema R0: `μ∗Λ = −μ·log`. Thm S (PROVED, incondicional): el centro de toda la familia rígida
    cambia de signo infinitas veces. Prop S2: `α = log X` es el único con centro sin polos dobles. Prop F: la única línea
    que usa la ecuación funcional es `C_0 = −2ζ′/ζ(½)`.
  - R4, Prop K (PROVED, sólo para modelos periódicos): el error pseudoaleatorio unilateral es `≥ (4−o(1))e^T/T`. Es la
    obstrucción de tipo Liouville.
  - R5:
    - Lema R (PROVED): la identidad del resonador.
    - Thm D / Cor D1 (PROVED, Karamata CITED): la positividad para todo T acota el residuo polar de un peine
      no negativo por 1, y Λ satura la cota.
